verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. The claim's observations are literally accurate but they describe leading whitespace only, which is an explicit reject criterion (formatting / page-break furniture), and the asserted consequence -- a flattened or misattached rule hierarchy -- does not survive inspection.

WHAT I CHECKED. Rendered spec_p82.png at 300 dpi and read it against E:/Temp/specrecon/v82/page-82.md, then confirmed the transcription lines in the canonical file E:/CobolSharp/specs/ISO_COBOL.md (page-82 block = lines 3618-3647). I also rendered and read page 81 (spec_p81.png, canonical lines 3588-3615) because the claim's comparison depends on it, and read forward to page 83 (lines 3650-3676) to see where the list ends.

BOTH QUOTES ARE ACCURATE. Grep confirms line 3623 is 'b) A format 1 REPLACE statement without the ALSO phrase ...' at column 0 and line 3610 is '   a) A format 1 REPLACE statement with the ALSO phrase results in the following:' with a 3-space indent, with '      1.' / '      2.' at 6 spaces on lines 3612/3614. The PDF indentation is as described: on the page image 8) begins at the left margin, a)/b)/c) and b)/c)/d) are inset one step, 1. through 4. a further step, and 'a. The two representations ...' a step beyond that. So the claim misquotes nothing.

WHY IT IS NOT A CONTENT DISCREPANCY.
(1) ZERO text is missing, altered, reordered, or attached to a wrong parent. I compared all thirteen printed blocks on page 82 against lines 3621-3645 word for word: b), c), d) of rule 7; rule 8) itself; a), b), c) of rule 8; sub-items 1., 2., 3., 4.; and the deepest item 'a. The two representations of the quotation symbol ...'. Every one is present verbatim, correctly labelled, in printed order, on the correct page. Nothing is misplaced, so the 'misplaced-content' kind is itself a misnomer -- this is at most an indentation-normalization inconsistency.
(2) THE HIERARCHY IS CARRIED BY THE ORDINAL LABELS, NOT BY THE INDENT. The chain 8) -> a)/b)/c) -> 1./2./3./4. -> a./b. is fully recoverable from the transcription: the letter and number sequences are unbroken and sequential, and c) ends in the colon 'The following rules apply for the purpose of matching:' that introduces 1.-4. A citation such as '7.2.4.4 GR 8) c) 1.' is derivable from the markdown exactly as from the PDF. Nor can 1.-4. read as 'an unrelated top-level ordered list': the only other top-level numbering in scope is the general-rule sequence, which is at 9) and 10) by the time this list closes (lines 3671/3673), so a restart at '1.' is unambiguously a nested list.
(3) THE TRANSCRIPTION STILL MARKS THE DEEPEST LEVEL. Line 3645 is '    a. The two representations ...' with a 4-space indent under '4.', so relative nesting is not uniformly discarded even on this page.
(4) IT IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE PLUS A DOCUMENT-WIDE EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-82 DEFECT. The b)/c)/d) that lose their indent are precisely the items that fall immediately after the page-81/82 break -- the classic page-break case the verification rules say to reject. And the pattern is pervasive, not local: across specs/ISO_COBOL.md there are 794 indented 'x) ' items versus 572 at column 0, so roughly 42 percent of all alpha list items sit at column 0. Flagging this one page as structural would imply hundreds of identical 'findings' elsewhere. The same flattening simply continues onto page 83 (d) through g) and 5., 6. at lines 3663-3669 are all at column 0), confirming it is a systematic whitespace-normalization behavior of the extraction, not lost content.

RESIDUAL. The internal inconsistency inside a single list -- a) indented on page 81, b)-d) flat on page 82 -- is real and is worth a cosmetic normalization pass over the whole transcription if the project ever wants indentation to be load-bearing. It is a document-wide tidiness item of cosmetic severity, not a page-82 structural content discrepancy, and no COBOL semantics can be misread because of it.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. Every element printed on PDF page 82 -- rule 7 items b), c), d); rule 8) and its items a), b), c); sub-items 1. through 4.; and the deeper item 'a. The two representations ...' -- is present verbatim, correctly labelled and in correct order at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 3621-3645. The only difference is leading whitespace: the extraction left these items at column 0 while page 81 kept a 3-space/6-space indent. The rule hierarchy is encoded in the ordinal labels and remains fully recoverable, and the deepest item retains a 4-space indent. The affected items are the first content after the page-81/82 break, and column-0 alpha items are a document-wide artifact (572 of 1366 across the file), continuing unchanged onto page 83. If tracked at all, this belongs as a cosmetic, document-wide indentation-normalization item, not a page-82 structural finding.
